system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: AnyTool is initiated upon receiving a queryQ, the function list detailed in Ta- ble 8, and a bootstrap prompt as outlined in Section B.1 of the appendix.
system_prompt_style.note: Quote spans line breaks in PDF text; mechanism of rendering not shown in evidence. Solver gets a new bootstrap prompt on reflection (Sec. 4.3).

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Each type of agent possesses its own distinct set of functions.
env_context_strategy.note: Agents explore API hierarchy via functions like get_tools_in_category, get_API_details.

context_compaction.note: Solver history cleaned of irrelevant API calls on reflection (Sec. 4.3), but no general compaction reported.

observation_format.evidence_quote: The results produced by these functions are subsequently incorporated into the historical context, which is then returned to the agents.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: AnyTool is powered by the function calling feature of GPT-4, eliminating the need for training external modules.

tool_count.note: Varies per agent type (Table 8); solver tools are the dynamic API-candidate pool plus finish.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: a solver aimed at resolving user queries using a se- lected set of API candidates
edit_primitive.note: API-calling agent; no file editing tools.

tool_schema_source.note: API schemas derived from ToolBench/RapidAPI documentation JSON.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: We leverage the API structure defined by Rapid API as a guideline.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: Two potential implementations for the solver are the Depth- First Search-Based Decision Tree (DFSDT) or the Chain of Thought (CoT) approach.
loop_primitives.note: Default DFSDT; self-reflection re-activates after GPT-4 judges unresolved.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: This arrangement is inspired by the divide-and-conquer ap- proach.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: The hierarchical structure includes a meta-agent linked with several category agents, each of which manages a collection of tool agents.
multi_agent_topology.note: Retriever hierarchy then single solver agent.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: a meta-agent exists, tasked with dynamically generat- ing a series of category agents in response to the user query

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: This process repeats contin- uously until the termination criteria are met.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: In addition, we record the historical context and sta- tus of each agent.
short_term_state.note: Global API candidate pool and agent Finished status.

self_verification.evidence_quote: Upon receiving a query, AnyTool suggests a solution, which is then evaluated for feasibility by GPT-4.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: this mechanism can be applied repeatedly until the termination condition is met.
retry_policy.note: Termination condition unspecified; Fig. 3 shows 4-6 rounds.

rollback.evidence_quote: we first remove these APIs from the expanded API-candidate pool and exclude items where these APIs are called from the historical context of the solver.
rollback.note: DFSDT backtracking is search, not environment rollback.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: This cycle continues until the solver gives a “Give Solution” or “Give Up” decision.
termination_condition.note: Retriever also stops when candidate pool is full (max_api_number).

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: We utilize over 16,000 APIs from Rapid API
execution_isolation.note: Actions are remote RapidAPI/ToolBench server calls.

tracing.evidence_quote: The pass rate can be found in the success_cnt.txt under the output directory.

target_domain.evidence_quote: a large language model agent designed to revolutionize the utilization of a vast array of tools in addressing user queries.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: Fill your OpenAI GPT-4 API config and toolbench key into the config.py
